records.name: Gerald B. Shreiber Pet Therapy Program at CHOP
records.summary: A pet therapy program at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. Trained volunteers and their dogs visit patients in the hospital.
records.what_you_do: Bring your own registered dog to visit patients at least once a month, in two-hour shifts, going room to room with the program coordinator's guidance.

schedule.text: Each volunteer team visits patients in two-hour shifts, with at least one shift a month.

cost.text: CHOP Volunteer Services covers the health clearances and background checks, and the dog screening at Penn's veterinary hospital is free to the owner. The page does not say whether routine vaccines, vet visits or registration fees are covered.

requirements.gear: A registered therapy dog aged 1 to 10 on a leash. CHOP provides the bandana the dog wears.

first_step.how: Read the program's requirements, then send the Application of Interest from its page. The coordinator emails within 5 to 7 business days to set an in-person interview, which you attend without your dog.
first_step.basis: An application, an interview, dog screening, health clearances, background checks and an orientation all come before the first visit, and the page offers no exemptions.
first_step.what_to_expect: The steps run in order: an in-person interview, dog screening at Penn's veterinary hospital, health clearances and background checks, then a two-hour orientation. On your first three visits the program coordinator goes with you. Each visit is a two-hour shift in which you and your dog go room to room to see children in a calmer, more homelike setting.
first_visit_tips: Wash your dog within 24 hours of a visit, and bring it in dry.
Skip flea and tick topical treatments for two days before a visit.
Keep your dog on a leash and out of strollers or carriers. It wears a CHOP bandana, which the program provides.
The page has no parking or check-in details, so ask the coordinator where to go on your first visit.

records.notes: The only dated item found is a news story published September 25, 2019. Status is kept probably_active because the program's own page is live and no newer dated item was found, but a reviewer may prefer dormant. The page names the Pennsylvania child abuse history and state police clearances plus FBI fingerprinting; act153_clearances is set true on that basis, though the page does not use the words Act 153. The page says volunteer spots at the King of Prussia hospital are full and the Philadelphia hospital needs volunteers (no year shown). Court and service-hours letters are not stated, so both are left unknown. Dog must be 1 to 10 years old and registered with one of four therapy dog groups, which are listed as leads.

records.name: Germantown Country Dancers
records.summary: A dance group that holds weekly English country dances, monthly workshops and dances, barn dances, and teen dances, with live bands, callers, and a Colonial performance group.
records.what_you_do: Come to a Wednesday dance or a barn dance with no partner needed. Musicians and sound volunteers are also welcome.

schedule.text: Wednesday English country dances, with a new dancer orientation at 7:30 pm. First Saturday afternoon workshop and evening dance, October to May, at Summit Presbyterian Church. First Sunday barn dances, November to April, for all ages. Teen dances for ages 12 to 19 on second Saturdays, October to May, at the same church.

locations.label: Summit Presbyterian Church, Mt. Airy (first Saturdays, barn dances, teen dances)
Merion Friends Meeting Activities Building (Wednesday dances)

cost.text: Wednesday dances are sliding scale, about $7 to $15 or more. First Saturday afternoon workshops cost about $10 to $15 or more, and evening dances about $15 to $25 or more. Barn dances cost $5 to $10 for adults and $3 to $5 for children and teens. Teen dances cost $5, or $10 to support the live music fund. Passes are available for anyone who cannot pay the listed price.

requirements.gear: Comfortable flat-soled shoes that will not slip on a wood floor

access.notes: Nearest SEPTA: Narberth station on the Paoli/Thorndale Line is about a 10 minute walk to the Merion building, and the 44 bus stops near its driveway. Upsal station on the Chestnut Hill West Line is about three blocks uphill from Summit Presbyterian Church, and the H bus stops one block away at Westview and McCallum.

first_step.how: Come to a Wednesday dance at the Merion building, arriving by 7:30 pm for the new dancer orientation. You do not need a partner.
first_step.basis: A short orientation for new dancers runs before the Wednesday dance, admission is drop-in, and passes are offered to anyone who cannot pay.
first_step.what_to_expect: The evening runs from a 7:30 pm orientation to dancing that ends around 10:15 pm. Every dance is taught before it is called, so you learn as you go, and partners change through the evening. Admission is on a sliding scale, and no experience or partner is needed.
first_visit_tips: Wear comfortable, flat-soled shoes that will not slip or catch on a wood floor.
Arrive by 7:30 pm for the orientation.
The Merion building sits back from Montgomery Avenue and is hard to see from the road. Look for the driveway with old-style street lamps.
At Summit Presbyterian Church, park on the uphill side of Greene Street only, and do not park on Westview Street.

records.notes: The group's events list shows dated 2026 events from October 3 to November 7, which set status and last_sign_of_life. The group's pages call the church Summit Church; its address page gives the full name Summit Presbyterian Church. The site says entry prices are higher starting in October (no year shown), so the cost text uses the figures as listed on the page. The group warns about fake emails asking for money in the names of board officers; confirm any money request with a board member in person. The site does not say whether the Wednesday dances have a sign-up step, so none is recorded.

records.name: Germantown Jewish Centre
records.summary: A congregation at 400 West Ellet Street that serves the Jewish community in Northwest Philadelphia. It runs Friday night services, weekly Torah study, adult learning, a religious school, a choir, and a Hazak group for people 55 and older.
records.what_you_do: Attend Friday night services, join Weekly Torah Study with the rabbi, take an adult class at Koleinu Beit Midrash, or join the men's club, Women of GJC, the choir, or Hazak. Families can enroll children in the religious school or early childhood program.

schedule.text: Friday night services at 6 pm. Saturday morning services, with separate adult services and children's programs, run from 10 am to about 12:30 pm. Weekday services are Monday and Thursday at 7:15 am and Sunday at 9 am. Weekly Torah Study with Rabbi Fredi Cooper meets Mondays at 1 pm on Zoom. Adult classes run each term, and about half are online.

cost.text: Membership dues are set in a conversation with each household, and the congregation says no one is turned away for money reasons. Adult classes are open to anyone, each class lists its non-member rate on its registration page, and scholarships are available to members on request.

access.notes: The adult classes page says to contact the associate rabbi about accommodations or access needs.

first_step.how: Call the office at 215.844.1507 or email office@germantownjewishcentre.org before you come, and ask to attend a Friday night service or a class. To start membership, use the online membership form.
first_step.basis: The join page says prospective members are welcome at a service or program after a call or email, and the adult classes page says anyone may take a class and gives a registration link for each.
first_step.what_to_expect: Friday night services start at 6 pm. Adult classes each have their own registration page, and about half of the fall classes are online, so you can try one from home. The site does not say what dress is expected or how long a service runs, so ask the office before your first visit.
first_visit_tips: Call the office before you come, since the site does not say whether non-members may attend Friday night services.
Saturday has separate adult services and children's programs, which run at different times.
The congregation is at 400 West Ellet Street, Philadelphia 19119.
If you sing, the all-volunteer choir rehearses Wednesdays from 7 to 9 pm and welcomes new members.

records.notes: The membership contact on the join page is community@germantownjewishcentre.org. The join page and the adult classes page name different people as Program and Membership Director, so no person is recorded. Weekly Torah Study registration closed June 30, 2026; the Monday 1 pm Zoom time is from its listing. Choir contact: rabbinicassistant@germantownjewishcentre.org or 215.844.1507 ext. 16. Hazak is for members 55 and older and has its own membership page. Accessibility and parking are not covered by the site. The fall 2026 to 27 class list is current, but its month is not shown, so last_sign_of_life uses the June 2026 Torah listing.

records.name: Germantown Masjid (Masjid as-Sunnah an-Nabawiyyah)
records.summary: A mosque on Germantown Avenue that runs free classes from Wednesday to Sunday, open to brothers and sisters. It also has an academy, an enrichment program and a weekly outreach booth downtown.
records.what_you_do: Come to a free class on any day from Wednesday to Sunday. The Sunday 10 am New Muslim class is for men and women. Ask about the youth enrichment program for ages 6 to 16 and the academy, a school next to the mosque. The mosque also runs an outreach booth in Downtown Philadelphia.

schedule.text: Free classes Wednesday to Sunday, taught by named teachers. Most classes start after one of the daily prayers, such as after Fajr, Asr, Maghrib or Isha. The New Muslim class meets Sundays at 10 am for men and women. Office hours are 10 am to sunset every day.

first_step.how: Go to the Sunday 10 am New Muslim class, or call 267-900-5371 to ask about the schedule and whether you need to register.
first_step.basis: A New Muslim class for men and women runs on Sundays at 10 am, and the classes are free and open to everyone, but the site does not say whether registration is needed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Classes are taught by named teachers, and each one is free. The New Muslim class meets Sundays at 10 am for men and women. The site does not say how long a class lasts, which room it uses or the language of instruction, so call ahead.
first_visit_tips: Call before you come, since the classes page lists no rooms, end times or language of instruction.
Office hours run from 10 am to sunset every day, so the office can answer questions during the day.
The site does not cover dress or parking, so ask about both when you call.

records.notes: The classes page lists 11 classes with named teachers, most after a prayer time. It gives no rooms, end times, language of instruction or registration step. The contact page gives the street address as 4944 Germantown Avenue, but the home page and the IRS record say 5020, so 5020 is kept and a person should check it. The enrichment program runs twice a year, summer and winter, for children aged 6 to 16, with a linked registration form; its question email is GtownMasjidcamp@gmail.com, which is not recorded as the masjid's email. The academy is a school next to the masjid with its own admissions contacts, listed as a lead. The dawah booth's day and place are not stated. The only dated items found are a 2026 copyright footer and the prayer times widget for October 4, 2026.

records.name: Germantown Monthly Meeting
records.summary: A Quaker meeting in Germantown that worships on Sunday mornings, in person or on Zoom. Its 2023 report describes a children's program for elementary-age kids and a monthly Sunday food distribution it hosts.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship at 10:30 am at the Coulter Street meetinghouse or on Zoom. Ask whether the monthly Sunday food distribution described in the 2023 report is still running, and ask about adult classes, which were restarting in 2023 with talks and a poetry reading.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10:30 am at 47 West Coulter Street, in person or on Zoom. Elementary-age children have First Day School in person, and childcare is offered for the youngest children.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:30 am. Call 215-951-2235 or email gmm@germantownmeeting.org with questions before your first visit.
first_step.basis: Worship has a set time and a listed phone and email, and the Yearly Meeting's 2023 report says a committee welcomes new attenders; the group's own site could not be read this run.
first_step.what_to_expect: Worship starts at 10:30 am on Sunday at the meetinghouse at 47 West Coulter Street. Children go to First Day School, and childcare is offered for the youngest. No cost is listed, and the 2023 report says worship was also offered on Zoom.
first_visit_tips: Call or email before you come, since the group's own site could not be read this run.
The building is wheelchair accessible, according to the Yearly Meeting's directory page.
If you want to help with the food distribution, ask whether it is still running, since the 2023 report is the only source for it.

records.notes: The group's own site (germantownmeeting.org) returned a TLS certificate error on two attempts, so no page of the group itself was read. Its facts come from a current Yearly Meeting directory page (Sunday 10:30 am, phone, email, wheelchair accessible; no Zoom mentioned) and a May 2023 Yearly Meeting report (hybrid Zoom worship, First Day School revived, monthly Sunday food distribution supporting the Center for Returning Citizens, adult classes restarting). The 2023 items are unconfirmed for 2026. A Philadelphia Quarterly Meeting save-the-date names this meeting as host of a gathering on January 24, 2027 (10:30 am to 4 pm); no posting date was shown, so last_sign_of_life is left empty. Status is probably_active because the directory listing is current and the 2027 gathering is planned, but the newest dated activity of the meeting itself is from 2023. A person should confirm current status by phone before this is treated as active.

records.name: Get Fresh Daily
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that sells locally grown produce through Black Farmers Markets and weekly produce boxes. It also keeps a garden open in West Philadelphia and runs wellness events and workshops.
records.what_you_do: Shop at the Black Farmers Market on the second and fourth Saturdays, order a weekly Fresh Takes box for $25, or visit the garden on Wednesdays and Thursdays during the season.

schedule.text: Black Farmers Market on the second and fourth Saturdays, 10 am to 2 pm. The garden is open April to November on Wednesdays and Thursdays, 12 to 6 pm.

locations.label: Freedom Greens + Gardens, 52nd Street Corridor (Black Farmers Market)

cost.text: Most produce at the market is pay-what-you-wish. Fresh Takes boxes cost $25 each and are ordered through the group's online Marketplace.

first_step.how: Visit the Black Farmers Market on a second or fourth Saturday between 10 am and 2 pm, at Freedom Greens + Gardens on the 52nd Street Corridor.
first_step.basis: The market and garden are open to the public on posted hours, and neither the group's pages nor the search listings mention membership or sign-up.
first_step.what_to_expect: The market sells fruits, vegetables, herbs and plant medicines grown by Black and Brown farmers, along with food makers and artisans. Most produce is pay-what-you-wish. The group's pages do not give the number of vendors or say what else happens on a market day, so check the group's social accounts before you go.
first_visit_tips: The group's pages do not list which payment methods the market takes, so ask at the stand.
The market is across from Malcolm X Park on the 52nd Street Corridor.
If you want to see the garden, it is open Wednesdays and Thursdays from 12 to 6 pm. The pages do not say whether visitors can join garden work.

records.notes: The group's own site lists no upcoming events on the date checked and shows no dated 2026 item. The 2026 market evidence comes from web search snippets (CraftMap, Food Trust map, Happening Next), which disagree on dates and hours, so the 52nd and Pine address and the July 25, 2026 market date are from listings, not the group's site. Status is active on that third-party listing; a reviewer may prefer probably_active. The site does not state the market season, box pickup or delivery, or whether garden visitors may join work. Fresh Takes box terms (length, billing) sit on a Marketplace page that was not read. One listing shows a 2026 season from mid May to early November, which is unverified. A 2025 vendor listing said EBT was accepted at a stand; current payment options were not confirmed. The contact page lists no phone or email, only social accounts.

records.name: Girls in Gear
records.summary: A cycling program for girls of all ages and abilities, with coaches who run group sessions to build confidence.
records.what_you_do: Girls can join a clinic or Club GiG, or find a ride near them. Coaches receive training in safety and the group's curriculum, and volunteers can use the coach link on the site.

schedule.text: Glide to Ride clinics run about two hours each for first-time two-wheel riders, on set dates listed on the Greater Philadelphia page. Club GiG is an eight week club for confident riders that meets on Saturday afternoons at various locations.

locations.label: Chamounix Tennis Courts, Fairmount Park (Glide to Ride clinics)

cost.text: The Greater Philadelphia page does not state fees or scholarships. The registration page says the group wants every girl to be able to join regardless of money, but it does not say how that works.

first_step.how: Choose a Glide to Ride clinic date on the Greater Philadelphia page and register through its link. To coach instead, email info@girlsingear.org.
first_step.basis: The Greater Philadelphia page lists a two hour clinic for first-time two-wheel riders with registration links, and the coach page says no cycling expertise is needed to coach.
first_step.what_to_expect: Glide to Ride is about two hours and is aimed at riders who are new to two-wheel cycling. Coaches run each group session with a focus on confidence and safety. The group's pages do not say what to bring, whether you need your own bike or helmet, or what the fee is, so check the registration page before you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Pick a clinic date on the Greater Philadelphia page; each date has its own registration link.
Check the registration page for fees and scholarship options before you sign up.
Ask the program director by email whether girls need their own bike or helmet, since the site does not say.

contacts.contact_name: Nikki Spector, Greater Philadelphia Program Director

records.notes: The Greater Philadelphia page lists 2026 clinic dates on October 3 and 17 and November 1 and 8, and Club GiG starting September 19, 2026 with registration open. The November 8 clinic is in Conshohocken, outside the city, so it is not in locations. The page shows no posting date and the October 3 date has already passed, so the listing may be partly stale; last_sign_of_life uses the September 19, 2026 Club GiG start. Coach page: coaches are adult volunteers except at Camp GiG, where they are paid; junior coaches aged 13 to 17 apply and train; interested people email the group, and that page has no online form. No page read gives an age range for the girls, so no minimum age is recorded. The Glide to Ride host, Friends of Chamounix Tennis Courts, is listed as a lead.

Budget: 33 fetches and 1 WebSearch (on Get Fresh Daily, whose own site has no dated 2026 items); not out of budget. No rate limiting seen. (5) Get Fresh Daily's active status rests on a third-party listing of a July 2026 market; its own events page lists nothing upcoming.
